clue.text: Ancient Scotsman curls first

indicators.note: first says the curls word comes before the Scotsman

parts.note: a perm is a hairdo that sets the hair in curls
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An elderly Scot has his hair curled ahead of anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts PERM ahead of IAN, though the clue names the Scotsman first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Permian is a geological period ending about 250 million years ago, so very old indeed.

clue.text: Designate European rescue vessel to guard strip of water

indicators.note: to guard means the first pieces surround and protect the inlet word

parts.note: Noah's ark rescued the animals from the flood
an arm of the sea is a narrow inlet

explanation.surface: An EU boat is assigned to patrol a channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescue vessel' is Noah's ark; 'strip of water' is an arm of the sea, not a coastal strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To earmark something is to set it aside or assign it for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Cutter heading to Malta with all on board P&O liner

indicators.note: the heading to a word is its first letter, here of Malta

parts.note: read the ampersand as and: the letters inside 'P and O liner', all carried on board it, are this run

explanation.surface: A slicer is sent to Malta along with everyone aboard a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the ampersand as 'and': pANDOLINEr holds the run.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandoline is a kitchen slicing tool with an adjustable blade, so it is a cutter.

clue.text: Commercial break lacking purpose

parts.note: an ad is a commercial on TV
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A TV advertising interval seems pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adrift means drifting aimlessly, without direction or goal.

clue.text: Embrace internet bride?

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in email and e-commerce
a bride is a newly married spouse

explanation.surface: Accept a mail-order bride found online?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that an e-spouse is an invented phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to embrace or adopt it.

clue.text: Gear for winter and spring workers

parts.note: to skip is to spring or hop
ants are the classic workers of crosswords

explanation.surface: Clothes suited to cold months and to the gardening season's labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season beside winter, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski pants are trousers worn on the slopes in snowy weather.

clue.text: Men embracing the alternative

indicators.note: embracing means the soldiers' letters hug the next word

parts.note: OR stands for ... ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers choosing a different option.
explanation.definitionFit: The other one is the alternative choice.

clue.text: Slav heading to exit after Poles receive "nul points"

indicators.note: after places the poles-and-zero block before the last letter
receive means the two poles take in the zero score between them

parts.note: S is the south pole
N is the north pole
Eurovision's zero score; zero is love in tennis

indicators.note: the heading to a word is its first letter, here of exit

explanation.surface: A Slav quits the Eurovision stage after the Polish entry scores zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' gives S and N, not Polish people; 'after' puts E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene, a native of Slovenia, belongs to the Slavic peoples.

clue.text: Change here can prompt renewal of cordial relations

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shift of approach here might bring about a thaw between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is a re-establishment of friendly relations, often between countries.

clue.text: He presses on in fury, close to despair

indicators.note: in puts the word on inside the anger word

parts.note: ire means anger or fury

indicators.note: the close to a word is its last letter, here of despair

explanation.surface: A man keeps going in a rage, nearly desperate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presses clothes with an iron is one who does the ironing.

clue.text: What those afraid of the dark want to stumble across

definitions.text: What those afraid of the dark want
definitions.meaning: people scared of darkness want a lamp switched on
to come upon something by chance

explanation.definitionFit: Read as three words it is a lamp left switched on; as a phrasal verb it means to find by chance.

clue.text: Gremlin in one's piano

parts.note: one's read as one is, said as I'm
p is the musical notation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: There's a mischievous sprite inside my piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a gremlin and an imp are small mischievous creatures.

clue.text: Furious with rotten fraudster

parts.note: mad means very angry
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Angry at a crook who is utterly corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernie Madoff ran a huge Ponzi scheme exposed in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Bernard Madoff was a notorious US swindler jailed for investment fraud.

clue.text: Colour of suit occupying writer

indicators.note: occupying means the suit word sits inside the writer word

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
to suit is to agree with, as in the food doesn't agree with me

explanation.surface: The shade of clothing an author is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea green is a bright yellowish-green shade like garden peas.

clue.text: Airborne gaggle of hidebound English

indicators.note: bound means the skin word ties up the English letter inside it

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: A flock of geese overhead are stuffy, conventional English types.
explanation.definitionFit: A skein is the term for wild geese in flight, a gaggle being geese on the ground.

clue.text: Inferior lyricist of appalling operettas

indicators.note: appalling suggests the word operettas is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A poor wordsmith who wrote dreadful light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trivial or bad verse.

clue.text: The ultimate in luxurious jewellery for the belly is staggering!

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter, here of luxurious

parts.note: tum is a colloquial word for the belly or stomach
bling is showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Showy navel jewellery is the height of luxury and simply astonishing!
explanation.walkthrough: 'staggering' looks like amazing but means tottering.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling and staggering both describe walking unsteadily.

clue.text: Garibaldi, perhaps, dropping it in his herbal tea

indicators.note: in puts the shortened biscuit inside the word his

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropping means the word it is taken out of the biscuit

parts.note: a Garibaldi is a British currant biscuit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garibaldi dunks his biscuit in his tea, perhaps losing it.
explanation.walkthrough: A Garibaldi is a flat British biscuit filled with currants; minus IT it is BISCU.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibiscus flowers are steeped to make a tart red infusion, a kind of herbal tea.

clue.text: Those prophesying doom of Corbyn back off, beginning to admire his alternative

indicators.note: back off means the rear letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn, former Labour Party leader

indicators.note: alternative signals a different arrangement of the letters before it
the beginning to a word is its first letter, here of admire

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doom-mongers turn against Corbyn, starting to admire his rival instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back off' removes Y from JEREMY; 'alternative' shuffles A and HIS into IAHS.
explanation.definitionFit: The prophet Jeremiah foretold disaster, so jeremiahs are pessimists predicting catastrophe.

clue.text: She prays alone before standing on bug

indicators.note: standing on in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a tiny insect-like bug

explanation.surface: A woman praying in solitude before treading on an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a religious recluse living alone, a hermit at prayer.

clue.text: Damn dogs chase Charles away

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs

indicators.note: away means the short name is removed from the word chase

explanation.surface: Blast, the dogs are chasing off Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: To damn someone and to curse them both mean to call down evil on them.

clue.text: Czech barman and I entranced by Stan Wawrinka's bottom

indicators.note: entranced by means the self word is held inside the following letters

parts.note: taken as written
me is the object form of I

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter, here of Wawrinka

explanation.surface: A Czech bartender and the narrator charmed by the tennis star's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: A composer is a 'barman', a writer of musical bars; Stan Wawrinka is a Swiss tennis player.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was a Czech composer, playfully a man who writes music in bars.

clue.text: Lower moral character between the sheets upset Home Counties

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: abed means in bed, lying between the sheets
the Home Counties around London lie in the south-east of England

explanation.surface: Bedroom antics upset the respectable suburbs and corrupt morals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, abbreviated SE for south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase someone is to lower their moral standing or degrade them.

clue.text: Iron Lady contrarily embracing little in the women's movement

indicators.note: embracing means the outer letters hug the small word

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: contrarily means the title is read the other way round

parts.note: Ms is a woman's title
mini means small

explanation.surface: Mrs Thatcher, contrary as ever, embracing a minor role in women's liberation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' looks like Margaret Thatcher's nickname, but the two words work separately; 'contrarily' reverses only the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Feminism is the campaign for women's rights and equality.

clue.text: Sidle round to bag lounger

indicators.note: to bag means the words capture the answer within their letters

explanation.surface: Edge round sideways to grab a sun bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounger is one who lazes about, a layabout.

clue.text: Resemble modern pound symbol

indicators.note: a pound is an enclosure, so the two words fence the answer inside

explanation.surface: To look like the new currency sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like part of 'pound symbol' but signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a badge or sign representing something.

clue.text: Finally wave bye-bye and go out

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of wave

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for a bye, so two byes give two Bs

explanation.surface: A last wave goodbye before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: When the tide ebbs it recedes or goes out.

clue.text: Boy is allowed pot for outdoor use

parts.note: Billy is a boy's name
can means may, is permitted

explanation.surface: A lad may take a cooking pot camping.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal tin used for cooking or boiling water over a campfire.

clue.text: Edges away from manic small creature

indicators.note: the edges of each word, its outer letters, are taken away

explanation.surface: A tiny creature edges nervously away from a frantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal is any living creature.

clue.text: Relief for the ailing socialist ideal after change of leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words swap their first letters

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
best means ideal, optimal

explanation.surface: A cure for the sick: socialism's utopia after new party leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of leaders' looks political, but swaps first letters of RED and BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed is prescribed to help a sick person recover.

clue.text: Notorious actress and oddly bleary FBI agent

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of bleary

parts.note: a G-man is a government agent of the FBI

explanation.surface: An infamous film star and a tired-eyed federal agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notorious' is the 1946 Hitchcock film, starring Ingrid Bergman, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid Bergman starred in Hitchcock's spy film Notorious alongside Cary Grant.
